properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency: hash.js@1.1.7 provides the SHA family (SHA-1/SHA-2) used by browserify-era crypto tooling in the JS test stack of this Solidity/JS monorepo. It ships whether or not application code calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the Ethereum transaction signature curve. The npm package (native bindings) plus its TypeScript types are declared dependencies; the test file uses secp256k1.Point.Fn.ORDER to construct a high-S signature and assert the contract rejects it (ECDSAInvalidSignatureS). Classical curve, quantum-unsafe, but fixed by the Ethereum protocol — not changeable here, only observable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey is a declared (transitive) dependency — the OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5 KDF in npm form, part of the crypto-browserify/browserify-desmac stack pulled in by the JS toolchain. It ships in the build; use depends on runtime paths.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test helper (first-party, changeable here) for the ERC-7913 smart-account tests: `RSASigningKey.random()` generates an RSA keypair (default modulusLength 2048, node:crypto generateKeyPairSync) and `RSASigningKey.sign`/`RSASHA256SigningKey.sign` sign a SHA-256 DigestInfo with node:crypto `privateEncrypt` — i.e. RS256 / RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SIGNING, the signature migration path (ML-DSA), not the key-transport path the record's ML-KEM remediation assumes. RSA-2048 is adequate classically but Shor-vulner

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 implementation shipped by the declared @noble/curves@1.4.2 dependency. Used indirectly via the JS test stack (ethers/viem ecosystem); Ethereum's signature curve. Observable here, fixed by protocol.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 22.12)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Release workflow helper (GitHub Actions, first-party): `isPublishedOnNpm()` calls global fetch() against https://registry.npmjs.com — a TLS session on Node/undici default settings with no cipher-suite or group configuration anywhere in scripts/, so the Node runtime's defaults decide key exchange. Node's default group list gained the hybrid X25519MLKEM768 only from 22.13/23.x, so on the declared floor (22.12) the connection negotiates classical ECDHE and recorded traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-la

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 implementation available via @noble/curves@1.4.2 — part of the JS test toolchain's crypto surface. No direct call site found in the application, but the library ships Ed25519 (classical, quantum-unsafe).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) implementation available via @noble/curves@1.4.2, pulled in for the JS test stack. OpenZeppelin 5.x added P-256/ERC-7913 support in Solidity (test/utils/cryptography/P256.test.js), so the JS-side P-256 curves are likely exercised in tests that mirror the Solidity P256 library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH implementation available via elliptic@6.6.1 (transitive dep). No direct call site in application code, but the library ships ECDH on classical curves — part of the crypto surface the build carries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is Ethereum's core hash (domain separation aside). Here it appears as the keccak npm dep, in foundry lint config referencing asm-keccak256, in generator scripts, and in ~50 test call sites via ethers.keccak256. Quantum-unsafe (Grover) but the algorithm is fixed by the Ethereum protocol — observable, not replaceable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@^3.0.17 plus @types/pbkdf2 declared in the lockfile. PBKDF2 is the standard password KDF — quantum-unsafe (Grover halves the key space) and used in the JS test stack for wallet/key derivation fixtures. Iteration count not visible at the lockfile level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@^3.0.0 declared in the lockfile — the scrypt password KDF in JS form (used for Ethereum keystore wallet derivation). Quantum-unsafe under Grover but parameterized by N/r/p which are not visible at the lockfile level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 available via @noble/hashes@1.4.0, a declared dependency. Part of the JS toolchain crypto surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 available via @noble/hashes@1.4.0. No direct call site in this repo's application code, but the shipped library provides the algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 available via @noble/hashes@1.4.0 — same algorithm family as Ethereum's keccak256, shipped in the JS toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM available via @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 (transitive dep). AES-GCM is a symmetric AEAD — quantum-vulnerable only in the key-search sense (Grover), otherwise the strongest symmetric AEAD commonly available.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD available via @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 (transitive dep) — strong symmetric AEAD, quantum concern is only Grover's key search.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/hashes@1.4.0 is the hash library in the JS toolchain (SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE, ripemd). Version 1.4.0 ships no post-quant algorithms — it decides what hash surfaces the build carries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/curves@1.4.2 is the elliptic-curve library used by test helpers (test/helpers/signers.js, ECDSA.test.js, P256.test.js). Version 1.4.2 ships classical curves only (secp256k1, P-256, Ed25519, etc.) — no PQ signatures — so it decides the project's classical-only signature posture in JS.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 ships symmetric AEAD (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Salsa). Transitive dependency in the lockfile; no post-quant concern beyond Grover key-search on symmetric crypto.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency: scrypt-js@3.0.1 declared in the lockfile — the scrypt KDF implementation shipped by the build (used by Ethereum keystore tooling). Same logical asset as ALG-c1f8b585 (scrypt algorithm), this entry records the library itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency: sha.js@2.4.12 — streaming SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations, declared in the lockfile as part of the browserify crypto stack. Ships SHA-1 (broken hash) alongside SHA-2.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency: elliptic@6.6.1 — classical elliptic-curve library (secp256k1/P-256/Ed25519 ECDH/ECDSA), declared in the lockfile. Ships only classical curves; quantum-unsafe. Same logical asset as ALG-c9ffc8a8 (ECDH via elliptic).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency: hash.js@1.1.7 — SHA family implementations, declared in the lockfile. Ships SHA-1 (legacy) and SHA-2. Same logical asset as ALG-50e53f84 (SHA family via hash.js).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency: pbkdf2@3.1.5 — the PBKDF2 KDF npm package, declared in the lockfile. Iteration count/salt are runtime parameters, invisible at lockfile level. Same logical asset as ALG-4de3b020 (PBKDF2).
